newsitem.title: POLAND: Pekpol mulls buying two meat firms.
newsitem.headline: Pekpol mulls buying two meat firms.

text.p: Polish food producer Pekpol SA is considering buying two or three meat firms next year as part of its plan to invest 25-30 million zlotys in 1996 and 1997, the firm's economic director said on Tuesday.

"We want to increase our production base and are mulling entering the privatisations of Zaklady Miesne Sluzewiec in Warsaw and Fabryka Oslonek Bialkowych in Bialka (southern Poland)," Krystyna Szpyrkowska told Reuters.
Szpyrkowska said 9.9 million zlotys for the investment came from its 1995 share issue, four million from depreciation, three million from profits and the rest from credit.
She said the investment would also go toward upgrading production at firms in its holding and building a hotel-restaurant and trade centre in the southern resort town of Zakopane.
Szypkowska said the firm planned investment of another 25-30 million zlotys from 1998 to 2000, for which an issue of shares or bonds could not be ruled out.
